meta._comment: Every region-specific input for the tools lives in this file. Adapted from Adam Gessaman's Pacific Northwest MeshCore Regions (https://gessaman.com/) for the Intermountain West mesh, with permission.
meta.name: Intermountain West MeshCore
meta.title: Intermountain West Repeater Zone Selector
meta.tagline: Search an address or click the map, pick a repeater type, and get ready-to-paste region commands.
meta.coverage: Covers ID, UT, and surrounding areas

hierarchy._comment_hierarchy: Parent chain is administrative only — it shapes the region put/def commands and the ancestry a node carries. Region scopes are matched per-tag in firmware, so the tree is for human legibility, not propagation.

_comment_seeds: PENDING. Region extent is being defined as polygons in GIS rather than weighted-Voronoi seeds; see the polygon resolver work. The tools will not run against this file until either seeds or a polygon layer is present — rankSeeds over an empty array leaves pool[0] undefined.

borders._comment: Polyline as [lon, lat] sorted ascending by lon; border(lon) is the latitude of the line at that longitude. A point with lat above border(lon) is on the 'north' side. mode 'hard' filters seeds to the point's own side; mode 'soft' only feeds crossBorderRules. The ID/UT line is a clean function of longitude (42 deg N from the NV corner to the WY corner), so it expresses exactly. NOTE: no rule below currently reads stateOrProvince — this is here so a future state-gated rule has something to classify against.

crossBorderRules._comment: Each rule: when ALL conditions in `when` hold, append `addTags` and `note`. Conditions: top2HasAll, primaryTagIn, primaryState/pointState, primaryCountry/pointCountry, repeaterTypeIn (evaluated only once a repeater type is chosen).
crossBorderRules.note: Northern Idaho dual-carries inw (the Inland Northwest community scope, shared with Spokane) and pnw (reach back into the Pacific Northwest mesh). Both are everyday carries, not high-site only.
Southwest Idaho dual-carries pnw — the Treasure Valley sits on the eastern Oregon corridor and affiliates with the Pacific Northwest mesh as well as the Intermountain West.
